claims.text: The proposed initial alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi produced by selective laser melting.
The as-processed CoCrFeMnNi alloy is initially single-phase.
Rapid solidification by SLM produces a fine cellular structure in this alloy.
The as-processed alloy contains uniformly distributed nanoscale Mn-containing oxide precipitates.
The relevant precipitates are Mn2O3-like particles located at cell or grain boundaries.
Moderate thermal cycling, sustained moderate-temperature exposure, or cyclic loading can drive precipitate coarsening and morphological evolution.
Fine boundary precipitates pin dislocations and hinder strain localization.
Precipitates growing beyond an optimal size provide less Orowan strengthening and forest hardening.
Coarsened precipitate interfaces act as local stress concentrators.
Loss of precipitate pinning and interfacial stress concentration promote intergranular or intercellular crack initiation.
Interfacial crack initiation caused by precipitate coarsening leads to a measurable loss of toughness.
This mechanism differs from conventional-alloy embrittlement, which is primarily caused by grain-boundary solute segregation.
Relative to the fine-precipitate baseline, samples with coarser precipitates will have lower fracture toughness and ductility.
Samples with coarser precipitates will exhibit earlier brittle-fracture features, including cracking along cell boundaries.
The as-processed SLM alloy has a favorable balance of high strength and ductility.
The baseline strength-ductility balance is caused by the fine, homogeneous precipitate structure.
Room temperature to approximately 700 °C is a relevant test range for identifying the onset of significant precipitate evolution.
The proposed mechanism operates when temperature and stress activate precipitate coarsening without causing complete recrystallization or other phase transformations.
The transition boundary depends on loading rate and thermal activation.
Oxygen availability can modify precipitate-growth kinetics.

contradictions.description: The material is repeatedly described as initially single-phase while also being described as initially containing a distributed population of Mn-containing oxide precipitates. Unless 'single-phase' is explicitly restricted to the metallic matrix, the precipitates constitute an additional phase.
